inputs.seed_note: no random numbers are drawn in P4

evidence_class: step 2 is independent of Stage 1 in the fuselage term (Multhopp's strip integral on the loft's width in place of Raymer's single factor) and partly independent overall: the wing and tail lift slopes and the lattice downwash are Stage 1's (spec 7.1c item 3). Step 1 is layout construction on the P3 arrangement. Step 3 (VSPAERO) is support, as under G-8. Step 4 is Stage 1's own equations with P2's measured section moment (a coding check plus one measured input). The power-on rows use a representative blade whose validation failed in P6 and carry no verdict

sources.why: Spec P4 step 2 asks for a fuselage-inclusive neutral point by a route other than Raymer's single factor (16.22): the fuselage moment slope integrated strip by strip over the loft's width with the wing's upwash and downwash (Multhopp), and the pusher propeller's normal force (Raymer (16.26) with Figs. 16.15 and 16.16). The library's notes do not hold those two figures at this aircraft's advance ratios and the book could not be opened in this session (its file is above the download limit of the Drive connector), so the propeller term uses the open NACA report that states the same method (thrust factor f times the zero-thrust normal-force derivative).

tm1036.title: Aerodynamics of the Fuselage
tm1036.author: H. Multhopp
tm1036.original: Luftfahrtforschung, vol. 18 (NTRS record: issue 2-3; the record's date is December 1942)

wrl25.number: NACA Wartime Report L-25 (NACA-WR-L-25), first issued as Advance Restricted Report L4I12a, October 1944
wrl25.title: Notes on the Propeller and Slipstream in Relation to Stability
wrl25.author: Herbert S. Ribner
wrl25.found_by: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/search?q=Notes on the propeller and slipstream in relation to stability

equation_3_7.as_read: (1/q) dM_R/d(alpha) = -(pi/2) * integral from 0 to l of b_R^2 (d(beta)/d(alpha)) dx
equation_3_7.symbols: M_R fuselage moment, q dynamic pressure, b_R fuselage width at the station x, l fuselage length, beta the local flow angle at the fuselage axis, alpha the angle of attack; per radian
equation_3_7.sign: The printed sign belongs to the report's moment convention. (3.11) shows the result is a forward shift of the neutral point (unstable). The code takes the size (pi/2) integral b^2 d(beta)/d(alpha) dx as a nose-up moment slope over q.

rule_for_d_beta_d_alpha.over_the_wing: 0 between the wing's leading and trailing edge at the fuselage (the flow is parallel to the chord)
rule_for_d_beta_d_alpha.behind_the_wing: rises linearly from 0 at the trailing edge to 1 - d(alpha_w)/d(alpha) (one less the downwash slope) at the fuselage stern near the tailplane
rule_for_d_beta_d_alpha.ahead_of_the_wing: greater than 1 (upwash); Fig. 8, computed for aspect ratio 8, 'or equivalent to a lift curve slope of 4.5'; for other aspect ratios 'converted approximately in proportion' to the lift-curve slope

equation_3_11.as_read: delta x_n / t = -(1 / (c_a' q F t)) dM_R/d(alpha)
equation_3_11.symbols: delta x_n forward shift of the neutral point, t wing chord, F wing area, c_a' lift-curve slope

table_1.what: Measured and computed shifts of the neutral point for seven aircraft: fuselages 2.0/2.3, 4.1/4.1, 9.2/9.4, 1.4/1.5, 2.0/2.0, 5.6/6.0, 4.0/4.4, 4.0/4.1 per cent of the chord (measured/computed). Not used as a test: the report gives no dimensions of those aircraft.

figure_2.what: Munk's factor K2 - K1 with the label (1/q) dM/d(alpha) = 2 (K2 - K1) Vol: the free moment of a slender body of revolution is twice its volume times q. With d(beta)/d(alpha) = 1, (3.7) gives (pi/2) integral b^2 dx = 2 Vol for a body of revolution; this is the closed-form test of the code.

figure_8.caption_as_read: Normal values for uprush before the wing. To the extent that the fuselage width is constant we put: integral from 0 to x of b_R^2 (d(beta)/d(alpha)) dx = x b_R^2 times the mean d(beta)/d(alpha)
figure_8.axes: abscissa x/t, the distance ahead of the wing leading edge over the wing chord, 0 to 2.4; ordinate 1 to 5
figure_8.curves: two: the local d(beta)/d(alpha), drawn from x/t 0.5 outward, and its mean from the leading edge out to x, (1/x) integral 0 to x, drawn from x/t about 0.1 to 1.05 (the local value 'reaches a fairly high peak in wing proximity', so only its integral is given there)
figure_8.how_read: First reading by eye on a 300 dpi enlargement at the grid lines. Second reading by pixel: the dark run of the curve in a column between two grid lines, converted with the grid lines found by pixel count (x/t 0 at 54 px, 595.4 px per unit; ordinate 1 at 980 px, 230.5 px per unit).
figure_8.not_read: Below x/t 0.15 the mean curve leaves the frame (it is at 4.6 near 0.1). The code takes the integral 0 to x as x times the mean, and straight to zero below the first reading.

method.pages: printed p. 6-7 (PDF pages 7-8); symbols printed p. 3-4 (PDF pages 4-5)
method.as_read: C_Y'psi = f C_Y'psi0: the derivative of the propeller normal-force coefficient (normal force over q and the disc area S', per radian of inclination of the thrust axis) is its value at zero thrust times a factor f that depends only on T_c = thrust / (rho V^2 D^2). f = 1 at T_c = 0.
method.same_as: Raymer (16.26), p. 428: F_p_alpha = q N_B A_p (dC_N_blade/d alpha) f(T). Raymer's Figs. 16.15 and 16.16 are 'after' this report's reference chain; here N_B (dC_N_blade/d alpha) is the report's C_Y'psi0 for the whole propeller.

equation_6.as_read: delta x / c_w = (S'/S) [ (8/pi) (z/c_w) dT_c/dC_L + f C_Y'psi0 (1 - d(epsilon)/d(alpha)) (l_1/c_w) (1/C_L_alpha) ]
equation_6.symbols: delta x forward shift of the neutral point by the direct propeller forces; S' disc area; S wing area; z thrust-line distance from the centre of gravity; l_1 distance from the centre of gravity to the propeller plane, positive for a tractor; epsilon the wing's downwash at the propeller
equation_6.use: The code puts the same normal force into Raymer's (16.9), which also carries it in the denominator. z is zero in r0 (hub on the centreline). (6) is used in the test as the first-order check.

equation_12.note: a is the inflow factor of the symbols page; its relation to T_c is in the report's reference 3 and was not opened. The code reads f from Fig. 1. The test checks Fig. 1 against (12) with the actuator-disc relation T_c = (pi/2) a (1 + a) (thrust = 2 rho A V^2 a (1 + a): Mattingly App. L (L.3) with the disc speed of (L.5), p. 610-611, taking the speed at the disc as V (1 + a)).

figure_1.how_read: First reading by eye on an enlargement at the grid lines; second by pixel between grid lines (T_c 0 at 607 px, 826 px per unit; f 1.0 at 1261.5 px, 825 px per unit, grid found near the read region because the scan is slightly turned).
figure_1.note: The point [0.0, 1.0] is the definition of f, not a reading.

figure_2.what: C_Y'psi0 against the blade angle at 0.75 R, 15 to 60 deg, Hamilton Standard propeller 3155-6 with a 0.164-diameter spinner, side-force factor 80.7; curves for 2, 3, 4 and 6 blades single rotation and 6 blades dual rotation. The three-blade curve was read.
figure_2.how_read: First reading by eye on an enlargement at the grid lines; second by pixel between grid lines (blade angle 0 at 648 px, 20.06 px per deg; ordinate 0 at 1421 px, 1990 px per unit).

equation_4.as_read: S.F.F. = 525 (b/D) at 0.3 R + 525 (b/D) at 0.6 R + 270 (b/D) at 0.9 R, 'accurate to about +-4 percent'

figure_6.what: Ratio of C_Y'psi0 of the desired propeller to that of the Hamilton Standard 3155-6 (S.F.F. 80.7) against the desired propeller's side-force factor, 50 to 120; one line per blade count. The three-blade line was read.
figure_6.how_read: First reading by eye at the line's end (S.F.F. 120); second by pixel in three columns, where the line S.F.F./80.7 drawn in the figure for comparison reads 1.302, 1.356 and 1.426 against 1.302, 1.354 and 1.425 computed.
figure_6.note: The point [80.7, 1.0] is the definition of the ratio, not a reading.

balance.h_cg_ft_note: The centre of gravity is on the fuselage reference line, as in Stage 1.

neutral_point.downstream_rule: linear from 0 at the root trailing edge to d(alpha_h)/d(alpha) at the tail's quarter mean chord, then constant to the end of the fuselage
neutral_point.bodies: The fuselage only. The sponsons lie inside the wing chord, where Multhopp's d(beta)/d(alpha) is 0, so (3.7) gives them nothing; Multhopp's nacelle term (3.10) is not applied. The turret and spinner are left out.
neutral_point.propeller_downwash_slope: the tail's d(alpha_h)/d(alpha) from the lattice is used at the propeller too (the hub is inside the lattice's wake sheet, where the lattice cannot be evaluated)
neutral_point.blade_for_side_force_factor: the P6 representative blade (PD-18): chords at 0.3, 0.6 and 0.9 R and the blade angle at 0.75 R of each point from runs/task12/pd/2026-11-27/p6/p6.json. P6 failed its validation row 5; only the blade's geometry and pitch are taken from it, and the power-on rows carry no verdict.

airfoil_cm0.source: P2 record runs/task12/pd/2026-11-27/p2b/p2.json (section moment about the quarter chord, NACA 4415 measured); the ledger has -0.08

propeller_clearance_ft.source: Least distance, along the axis, from the propeller plane forward to any part of a tail surface inside the propeller disc's radius. A judgement: the library gives no number (Raymer p. 222-223 says only that a propeller behind a wing should be mounted as far behind it as possible). 1 ft is about 0.15 propeller diameters and leaves room for the blades' deflection and the elevator's trailing edge. Solved at the band ends as a sensitivity

r1.tail_volume_coefficients: kept: horizontal c_ht times r0's ht_volume_scale, vertical c_vt (Raymer (6.28), (6.29), p. 111); the areas grow as the arm shortens. Aspect ratios and tapers kept.
r1.tail_trailing_edges: straight (all the taper on the leading edge), both tails. Added on 2026-11-27 after a trial of the methods, before any recorded run: with r0's planforms the solution does not exist (PD-20). The first form is still solved in the record.
r1.wing_position_rule: Stage 1's own rule: the mean of the full-fuel and empty-fuel static margins (payload on, gear up, nominal empty weight) is 0.10 MAC, the middle of R13, here with the independent neutral point, power off.
r1.main_gear_rule: Stage 1's own rule: the main wheels are the tipback angle (15 deg) behind the aftmost centre of gravity with the gear down (Raymer p. 232). The nose wheel stays at r0's station.
r1.weights: Tail weights by Raymer (15.47) and (15.48) (area to the 0.896 and 0.873; the tailplane's quarter-chord sweep terms; the fin weighed unswept, as Stage 1 weighs r0's) and the fuselage by the tail-arm term of (15.49) (L_t^-0.051), as ratios on r0's component weights, p. 404; nothing else changes and the aircraft is not re-sized (the take-off weight moves by the same pounds).

scan.tail: no arm puts the tail clear with the volume coefficients kept

r0_tail_planforms_clear_of_disc.reason: no wing position between r0's and 3 ft aft of it gives a mean static margin of 0.10 (f(a) and f(b) must have different signs)

acceptance.what: static margin at the full-fuel and empty-fuel centre of gravity, independent neutral point, power off: inside R13's 0.05 to 0.15 MAC
independent neutral point against Stage 1's: within 0.03 MAC
every loading of step 1 between the forward limit (trim and rotation) and the aft limit (neutral point less 0.05 MAC)
nose-wheel load at every loading inside 5 to 20 %
if 1, 3 or 4 fails: the wing position that restores them, for r1 (with the tail of PD-20)

findings_for_r1: On r0 with the P3 arrangement the static margin is 0.0607 full and 0.0374 empty of fuel (gear up, independent neutral point at 12.544 ft, power off): R13 (0.05 to 0.15) fails.

Fuselage term: Multhopp on the loft gives C_m_alpha 0.1831 per rad against Raymer (16.22)'s 0.1014; the neutral point is -0.0131 MAC from Stage 1's method. r1 should carry the fuselage term of this package.
On the r1 layout the two fuselage terms differ by -0.0148 MAC in neutral point (independent less Stage 1's method).
Wing for r1: leading edge at the root from 9.163 ft to 10.079 ft (+0.915 ft).

Tail for r1 (PD-20): arm from 13.577 ft to 11.132 ft (-2.445 ft), 0.3895 of the fuselage length against Stage 1's 0.475; tailplane 135.48 to 165.24 ft^2, fin 37.08 to 45.23 ft^2 (volume coefficients kept); trailing edges straight; every tail point inside the disc 1.00 ft ahead of the propeller plane.

The tailplane of the r1 layout is 0.611 of the wing area and its root leading edge is 1.06 ft behind the wing's root trailing edge (5.57 ft in r0). The methods used here (lattice downwash at the tail's quarter chord, Multhopp's linear rise behind the wing, a tail lift slope for an isolated surface) were not made for a tail this large and this close; the layout closes on paper and is a risk for Gate C.
Main wheels for r1: 14.045 ft to 14.734 ft (tipback rule); nose wheel unchanged.
Weights for r1 by Raymer (15.47)-(15.49): tailplane +18.81 lb, fin +5.83 lb, fuselage +2.29 lb; empty weight +26.93 lb (the aircraft was not re-sized).
With these the static margin is 0.0966 full and 0.1034 empty (row 1 pass); payload-on loadings outside the envelope: 0 of 132; nose-wheel load 13.9 to 15.1 % with the payload on.

Rotation with P2's section moment (-0.0911 against the ledger's -0.08): the tail needs 0.8128 of 1.00 on r0 as arranged and 0.9862 on the r1 layout (pass). r1 should run Stage 1's tail loop with the measured section moment.

Payload off: the centre of gravity goes as far aft as 14.938 ft (static margin -0.2729) on the r1 layout; 132 of 132 payload-off loadings are outside the envelope. Flight without the payload needs 420 lb of ballast at the payload station (an operating limit, PD-13).
Nose-wheel load on the r1 layout with the payload on: 13.9 to 15.1 %; 11 of the gear-down loadings are outside Raymer's 8 to 15 % optimum (item 31).
Empty-weight band (NR-14) on the r1 layout: static margin 0.1064 / 0.1179 at 0.95 and 0.0874 / 0.0899 at 1.05 (full / empty).

Power on (no verdict): the propeller's normal force moves the neutral point aft by 0.0048 MAC at loiter and 0.0077 MAC in the sea-level climb on the r1 layout; slipstream effects on the tail are not modelled.

For P9, not answered here: the sponson that does not hold the retracted main gear (P3 finding 7; the main wheels move with this package); where the tail roots sit on the engine bay; Stage 1 needs the tail arm as an input.
